sample_unit: model-question observations (150 MedQA-USMLE questions x 6 LLMs)

links.outcome: Explanation robustness to paraphrases and consistency across repeated queries (ESI, PSS) in LLM clinical answers
links.effect: Answer consistency negatively predicted causal faithfulness (Spearman r = -0.466); only 23.3% of cited concepts were causally necessary, showing consistency checks alone miss unfaithful reasoning.
links.quote: answer consistency negatively predicted CFS (Spearman r = -0.466)

links.outcome: Whether exam-style accuracy reflects faithful reasoning in LLMs
links.effect: Correct answers had lower CFS than incorrect answers (0.212 vs. 0.398); only 23.3% of cited concepts were causally necessary.
links.quote: Correct answers had lower CFS than incorrect answers (0.212 vs. 0.398)

unlisted_practices: Concept-ablation causal faithfulness score (CFS) for evaluating LLM explanations
Cross-model agreement of cited reasoning concepts as a safety signal

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluation of LLM faithfulness and explanation reliability on medical exam questions (MedQA-USMLE) using concept ablation and perturbation metrics, rather than testing a specific clinical deployment safeguard.
